newsitem.title: GERMANY: Chemicals star as German shares hit new records.
newsitem.headline: Chemicals star as German shares hit new records.

text.p: Chemical shares were the stars of the day on the German share market as they emerged from a long period of consolidation to lead the blue chip DAX index to fresh record highs.

Broad market gains were supported by a firm dollar, rising Bunds and overnight gains on Wall Street, but an advance of more than four percent on Bayer AG stock and more than three percent on Hoechst AG stood out.
At 1407 GMT in post-bourse screen trading, the 30-share IBIS DAX index was past the key 3,100 point level at 3,103.69 points, up 1.2 percent.
March DTB DAX futures were up 36 points at 3,114.0.
Apart from airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG, which surged more than five percent after the carrier announced the final stage of a restructuring programme, the chemical sector was the clear outperformer.
Dealers said chemicals were finally back in vogue after consolidating for nearly two months while the DAX surged.

The DAX 100's chemical sector index, which includes chemical stocks on the DAX-30 and the 70-share mid-cap MDAX, rose two percent in bourse trade, twice as fast as the DAX-100 as a whole, which rose 0.9 percent at 1,577.99.

"It had to happen some time," remarked a dealer at a major foreign bank in Frankfurt. "We have had chemicals back on our buy list since last week -- it didn't make sense that they all peaked last year."

While the DAX index has surged some eight percent since early December, chemicals have been lagging behind, even after today's gains. Hoechst for example is trading well off its December high of 73.40 marks.
Hoechst was up 2.47 marks at 71.82 marks at 1423 GMT while BASF was up 1.33 marks at 60.68, also well below its December high of 62.48 marks.
Dealers said there were more gains in store for the German chemical sector but were less confident about the broader market's direction.

"We made it over 3,100 (IBIS DAX points) which is a relief but that's just a number. The trick will be defending it (this key level) and there are a lot of other factors at play, especially Wall Street," a dealer said.

The market was likely to be stymied as usual in early trade Thursday before the Bundesbank's regular council meeting on that day, although there was little speculation that the central bank would take any action on interest rates.
Among other highlights of the day, Lufthansa remained ahead in later dealings and was up 5.3 percent at 23.37 marks.

Analysts gave a cautious welcome to its announcement of internal restucturing steps, although they said any savings for the airline were likely to be small and that Lufthansa's shares would likely come under pressure when the airline reports what are certain to be weaker earnings for 1996.
Dealers said Lufthansa's stock had partly risen for technical reasons, after an early upward push broke some key resistance levels.
